front.title: Enhancing ICMP Error Message Validation Using a Challenge-Confirm Mechanism

abstract.t:
ICMP error messages provide feedback used by hosts to manage network communication. Existing validation of the quoted invoking packet is essential, but its resistance to blind off-path forgery depends on the information quoted and the communication state available to the receiver.
This document describes a Challenge-Confirm mechanism that supplements existing ICMP validation. After an eligible initial error passes existing checks, the host can mark the associated flow and include an unpredictable token in an IPv4 option of a subsequent packet that would otherwise be transmitted. Receipt of the initial error does not immediately generate a probe or a separate ICMP Echo Request. A later ICMP error can return the token by quoting the invoking packet.
The token is computed using a secret local to the validating host. No key is shared with routers or peer hosts, and no per-challenge nonce cache is required. Successful token validation provides evidence of access to a valid token; it does not authenticate a router's identity or the semantics of the reported error. This document specifies bounded triggering, replay limitations, and deployment considerations, including the need to evaluate IPv4 option traversal and quotation. It does not report Internet-wide deployment measurements.
